brief.title: Amazon Bestselling Books: Price vs. User Rating Trend Analysis (2009–2019)
brief.one_liner: A comprehensive analysis of how book pricing strategies relate to customer satisfaction across Fiction and Non-Fiction genres over a decade of Amazon bestseller data.
brief.goal: The reader should understand whether higher-priced books achieve better user ratings, how pricing and rating patterns differ between Fiction and Non-Fiction, which authors and price segments dominate the bestseller list, and how these dynamics have evolved from 2009 to 2019 — enabling data-informed decisions for pricing strategy and catalog curation.

required_sections.title: Bestseller Market Overview (2009–2019)
required_sections.objective: Provide a high-level summary of the dataset: total books, genre split, average price, average rating, and review volume across the full decade.

required_sections.title: Price vs. User Rating: Correlation Analysis
required_sections.objective: Quantify and visualize the relationship between book price and user rating. Determine whether higher prices are associated with higher or lower ratings, including statistical correlation metrics.

required_sections.title: Fiction vs. Non-Fiction: Pricing and Rating Strategies
required_sections.objective: Compare average price, user rating, and review counts between Fiction and Non-Fiction genres. Highlight key differences and identify which genre delivers better perceived value.

required_sections.title: Year-over-Year Trends in Pricing and Ratings
required_sections.objective: Analyze how average book prices, user ratings, and review volumes have changed annually from 2009 to 2019. Identify inflection points or notable shifts.

required_sections.title: Dominant Authors on the Bestseller List
required_sections.objective: Identify authors who appear most frequently on the bestseller list across the decade. Analyze their pricing patterns and average ratings to understand what drives sustained bestseller status.

required_sections.title: Strategic Recommendations
required_sections.objective: Synthesize findings into actionable pricing and positioning recommendations for publishers and retailers targeting the Amazon bestseller list.

kpis.name: Average User Rating
kpis.description: Mean customer rating (0–5 scale) across all bestselling books, segmented by genre and year.

kpis.name: Average Book Price
kpis.description: Mean retail price of bestselling books, segmented by genre and year.

kpis.name: Price-Rating Correlation Coefficient
kpis.description: Pearson correlation coefficient between book price and user rating across the full dataset.

kpis.name: Average Review Count
kpis.description: Mean number of customer reviews per book, indicating engagement level and popularity.

kpis.name: Author Bestseller Frequency
kpis.description: Number of times an author's book(s) appeared on the annual top-50 bestseller list over the decade.
